Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps on GPU lane economics

Hi Lydia — thanks again for a great call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Need confirmation of target throughput: you mentioned 150 req/s steady-state with peaks to ~300 req/s for nightly reprocessing. Please confirm nominal Avg tokens per request (you said ~1.2k tokens).
- Budget band: you gave a $20k–$40k/mo infrastructure target. I noted you want cost per 1M tokens to land roughly between $18–$35 depending on latency SLAs.
- GPU preference: you called out wanting a cost/latency tradeoff — do you have a hard preference for A100-like performance vs cheaper H100-quantized lanes?
- Compliance: procurement will need a short security packet (SOC2 basics + network requirements). Camila will own assembling those docs.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You confirm avg tokens/request and steady/peak req/s numbers by end of week.
2) We’ll produce an initial pricing estimate (unit $/1M tokens, plus reserved-lane SKU suggestions across two GPU types) — see attached stub.
3) If numbers align, procurement loop-in and 30% trial reservation for 1 month.

I attached a lightweight pricing workbook (pricing_estimate_v1.xlsx) with two lanes: H100-quantized and A100-high-throughput, plus ballpark monthly totals for the throughput profiles you described. Camila — I’m looping you to pick up the compliance packet.

Thanks — talk soon.

Markus Klein

From: Lydia Barnes <lydia@hedgelabs.ai>

Cc: procurement@hedgelabs.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps on GPU lane economics

Thanks Markus — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Avg tokens per request: 1,250 tokens (range 300–5,000; 95th percentile ~2,800).
- Traffic profile: steady-state 140–160 req/s; predictable nightly batch bursts up to ~320 req/s for model refresh and reranks.
- Latency sensitivity: for our primary inference path we need 99p latency <= 350ms; secondary offline/batch jobs can be higher.
- Budget: leadership has allocated a $30k/mo target for infra during pilot; room to scale to $45k/mo if unit economics show clear savings.

On GPU preference: we prefer leaning towards more cost-efficient quantized lanes if they meet the 99p latency target for our 1.25k token median. If not, we'd consider a mixed lane (small percentage on A100-like VM for low-latency requests).

Procurement is looped in — they will share an internal PO template and are starting a security questionnaire.

-Lydia
Lydia Barnes
Head of ML Platform, HedgeLabs
lydia@hedgelabs.ai

Subject: Pricing sketch + GPU lane recommendations (HedgeLabs pilot)

Lydia — thanks for the rapid details, that helps. Attached is a slightly expanded estimate (pricing_estimate_v1.xlsx) plus a short note on network/arch items (network_requirements.pdf). High-level summary below: 

Summary unit economics (ballpark) for your profile (1.25k median tokens, 140–160 req/s, peaks to 320 req/s):
- H100-quantized lane (aggressive quant): ~ $22 / 1M tokens (estimated) — 99p latency for median requests ~ 280–320ms; 99p for 5k token requests may stretch beyond 350ms depending on batching.
- A100-high-throughput lane (higher perf, less quant): ~ $34 / 1M tokens (estimated) — 99p latency for median ~ 180–220ms; reliable headroom for 5k token tails.

Recommended pilot configuration:
- Reserved lanes: 8 GPU-equivalent H100-quantized units for steady throughput (should cover 140–160 req/s with continuous batching and KV cache).
- Burst pool: 2 A100-like instances to absorb peaks and low-latency traffic.
- Autoscale policy: aggressive prefix-KV cache + continuous batching for background jobs; route 85% of steady traffic to the quantized lane, 15% to A100 lane for high-priority requests.

Estimated monthly cost (infrastructure only, excluding support/license):
- H100-quantized lane (8 units): ~$18,500/mo
- A100 burst pool (2 units): ~$9,200/mo
- Total estimated infra: ~$27,700/mo (aligns with your $30k pilot target)

Notes / open items:
1) We need to validate 99p latency at your real payload distribution. If you’re open, we can run a short two-day stress run on a sample dataset to measure 99p at 1.25k median with both lanes.
2) Procurement: Camila will send the SOC2 stub and network_requirements.pdf. Procurement, can you share the PO template and any required contract clauses?
3) Trial reservation mechanics: we recommend a 30% reservation for 30 days to lock pricing and capacity; details in the attached workbook.

I’m happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow to walk through the workbook. If this looks reasonable, I’ll open a trial reservation and get Camila to attach the compliance pack.

Thanks — M

--
Markus Klein
